[32531 Global Information Systems | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject explores how globalisation has redefined information systems to support international business operations, including alliances and joint ventures. You'll examine the global IT industry's trajectory and structure, the strategic value of IT in business, and the impact of e-commerce, customer relationship management, knowledge management, outsourcing, and offshoring. Legal considerations in the digital economy for formalising business relationships are also addressed. Emphasis is placed on organising business information, with particular attention to informal flows within organisations. You'll learn about varying work types, team formation, and management processes, alongside practical skills in using portals and other tools to build relationships, maintain customer loyalty, and manage outsourcing partnerships.

[32531 Global Information Systems | Learning and teaching activities]
Global Information Systems is run as a three hour discussion with group activities. It is taught by a combination of classes, discussions and group activities based on case studies.

 Most weeks the tutorial sessions will consist of three main activities: (1) questions and/or exercises relating to that
 week’s class material; (2) student discussions that will be assessed (see "Contribution to Discussion" in the section on
 Assessment); and (3) guidance and assistance with understanding the concepts covered in classes and tutorials. Time will be available during the tutorials for students to ask specific questions regarding the class or tutorial aspects of the subject. Verbal feedback will be given each week to guide and inform learning. Tutorials will commence in week 3. Details of tutorial allocations will be provided in week 2. Students are required to access and use the weekly pre-class materials on Canvas as a sense making exercise attempting to create questions and explanations that will be used in class.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32531 Global Information Systems | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Analyse the legal and cultural issues and implications related to implementation of global information systems to a range of products and services. (B.1)
SLO2: Evaluate the effect and relationship of disruption and sustainability of technologies people and businesses within the global environment. (B.1)
SLO3: Analyse information processes and management structures arising out of conducting business within the global environment. (D.1)
SLO4: Explain the characteristics of global information systems and their role in business to a diverse range of people. (E.1)
SLO5: Collaboratively work in defined roles to produce design solution to complex problem. (E.1)
